noveltyJustification: This iteration resolves the missing-form frontier into three compact additions and separates stable checker contracts from per-template judgement, which the previous four angles did not settle.
keyQuestions: Which missing micro-forms earn a place, and which enforceable rules belong in the checker?
answeredQuestions: Add one spark capability with line, area and bar variants, plus tracker and bar-list. Keep KPI delta as optional anatomy, retain the existing progress and countable-ring answers, and enforce stable shared contracts while leaving question-fit and visual judgement per-template.
ruledOut: Adding progress-circle or radial-ring as new catalog questions solely from gauge and ring imagery.
Treating KPI delta as a sixth universal card part or a standalone chart id.
Adding three unrelated catalog rows for spark line, spark area and spark bar.
Replacing bar-rows semantics with a new palette or external implementation merely to reproduce a bar-list capture.
Making the checker judge headline quality, guide density, metric eligibility or radial worth.

title: The missing frontier is compact capability, not full-size catalog coverage
summary: The 26 current rows cover the principal quantitative question families. The local references expose compact monitoring and context forms that are not represented as catalog rows, so additions should be limited to distinct compact questions or contracts.

title: Spark earns one capability with line, area and bar variants
summary: The references show a low-height trend paired with a primary value and delta. It is a compact reading mode rather than a replacement for daily-line, and the three mark choices should share one spark question rather than become unrelated gaps.

title: Tracker earns a discrete status-over-time form
summary: Equal status blocks answer whether each period was healthy, missing or exceptional. That is distinct from a numeric daily line and a full-year quantity grid, and it can reuse the existing categorical role.

title: Bar-list earns a compact ranked-list variant
summary: In-bar labels and right-edge values create a stable compact density contract for long names. The question remains comparison, so the addition should share bar-rows semantics and palette rather than start a new family.

title: KPI delta belongs to optional card anatomy
summary: A primary value and meaningful baseline delta improve forms whose data supplies them, but progress-single and unit-ring already answer goal progress and countable part-to-whole. A progress-circle or radial-ring row would change shape without adding a distinct question.

title: Existing checker assertions cover the stable shared contract
summary: Document, card, geometry, palette, data, catalog and interaction assertions can catch concrete drift in new forms: missing parts, unapproved type or radius, geometry mismatch, literal colours, failed theme gates, index drift, prefilled cards, locale formatting, missing table values and unreachable marks.

title: Only explicit new contracts justify new checker assertions
summary: A proposed mark-policy assertion could require point, curve, fill and meaningful-zero declarations, and a proposed tooltip-indicator assertion could match indicator kind to mark kind. Headline quality, metric eligibility, guide density, hue robustness and radial worth remain review judgement.

direction: Adding progress-circle or radial-ring as new catalog questions solely from gauge and ring imagery.
reason: The current progress-single and unit-ring forms cover the existing questions, while the inspected radial captures do not add a distinct data contract.

direction: Treating KPI delta as a sixth universal card part or a standalone chart id.
reason: Metric and delta are useful only when a data-backed baseline exists, so they belong to optional anatomy around an existing chart question.

direction: Adding three unrelated catalog rows for spark line, spark area and spark bar.
reason: The references present the marks as variants of one compact trend role, not three independent reader questions.

direction: Replacing bar-rows comparison semantics with a new palette or external implementation merely to reproduce a bar-list capture.
reason: Bar-list changes label placement and compact density while preserving the comparison question and existing colour contract.

direction: Making the checker judge headline quality, guide density, metric eligibility or radial worth.
reason: Those choices require question and visual review, and the contract explicitly excludes headline and by-eye picture judgement from static assertions.
